items.title: YouTube introduces a new mute button on mobile, but not everyone is happy
items.summary:
TL;DR 

YouTube is rolling out a dedicated mute button within its mobile video player, letting users silence videos without adjusting their device’s volume. 
 Some users are frustrated by the button’s placement, reporting accidental presses when trying to skip forward in videos. 
 The feature appears to be rolling out gradually. We have it on iOS, but not on Android. 

YouTube is finally giving users on its mobile apps an easier way to outright silence video without having to fiddle with their device’s volume controls, and it’s manifesting in the form of a dedicated mute button . Although the new button does sound like a welcome addition, many users are already finding the change frustrating , mainly because of accidental presses.

The quality-of-life change doesn’t appear to be entirely new. We found a Reddit post from early October highlighting the mute button, suggesting that the streaming giant has been experimenting with it since then, at the very least. However, more recent reports indicate that the button is now making its way to a lot more users simultaneously (thanks @GreenShades9 ).
items.t: YouTube introduces a new mute button on mobile, but not everyone is happy

items.title: Amazon is ending software support for the 10th-gen Kindle and Paperwhite
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Amazon is ending software support for the 10th-generation Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite. 
 Both e-readers should continue working normally, with access to downloaded books and the Kindle Store remaining unaffected for now. 
 Amazon previously discontinued Kindle Store support for devices released in 2012 or earlier, but there’s no confirmed cutoff date for these newer models. 

One of the best things about owning a Kindle is that you don’t have to replace it every few years. As long as the screen works and the battery holds up, even an older model can serve you well. Unfortunately, if you’re still using a 10th-generation Kindle or Kindle Paperwhite, there’s some disappointing news.

As first spotted by Good e-Reader , Amazon is ending software support for both e-readers . The 10th-generation Kindle, released in April 2019, and the Kindle Paperwhite, which arrived in November 2018, will no longer receive software updates, including security patches.
items.t: Amazon is ending software support for the 10th-gen Kindle and Paperwhite

items.summary:

Live notifications on Galaxy devices are part of the Now Bar and offer continuous updates from supported apps directly on the status bar. According to “early Galaxy S27 series software” accessed by SamMobile , One UI 9.5 will include a new Live notifications chip positioned towards the top-center of the screen, similar to Apple’s Dynamic Island. items.title: Galaxy S23 Ultra root module adds AirDrop and 18 other features from newer Galaxy phones
items.summary:
Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

A developer has released a KernelSU module (s23-ultra-tweaks) that enables AirDrop compatibility and several Galaxy S24 features on a rooted Galaxy S23 Ultra running One UI 9 based on Android 17. 
 The mod injects Galaxy S24 Wi-Fi drivers, firmware, and other code at runtime to utilize the S23 Ultra’s existing Qualcomm WCN7850 chip without modifying system partitions or tripping Knox. 
 The project is in early stages, requires root access (which can break banking apps), and AirDrop compatibility has only been tested for outgoing transfers on a Canadian SM-S918W model. 

Samsung left AirDrop compatibility off the Galaxy S23 series when it rolled out One UI 8.5 earlier this year, frustrating owners who argued the phone’s Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 hardware was more than capable of handling it. Now, a developer has demonstrated that the Galaxy S23 Ultra can indeed run AirDrop alongside a slate of Galaxy S24 features, all without flashing custom ROMs.

Developer dtechterminal has released a KernelSU module called s23-ultra-tweaks that activates newer Galaxy features on a rooted Galaxy S23 Ultra running One UI 9 based on Android 17 . According to the project’s documentation, the Galaxy S23 Ultra shares the same Qualcomm WCN7850 Wi-Fi chip as the Galaxy S24 Ultra, which supports the Qualcomm “Wondertap” feature needed for Apple’s peer-to-peer Wi-Fi protocol (AWDL). However, the developer notes that the S23 Ultra’s stock “firmware, driver and system image leave all of this out.”
items.t: Galaxy S23 Ultra root module adds AirDrop and 18 other features from newer Galaxy phones

items.title: Samsung prepares Scam Detection and deepfake alerts for calls on WhatsApp, Telegram, and more
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 shows Samsung is extending its Scam Detection feature to third-party calling apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, Google Meet, and KakaoTalk. 
 One UI would soon warn you about scam conversations, known scammers’ voices, and AI-altered (deepfake) voices during these calls, with the analysis done on your phone. 
 The code points to South Korea first, with separate code for China. Samsung hasn’t announced these Scam Detection features yet. 

Samsung has been fighting phone scams on two fronts. In South Korea, One UI 8 brought voice phishing detection to the Phone app, while the Galaxy S26 series picked up Google’s Scam Detection in other markets. Both only protect regular phone calls, though. Scammers have adapted, moving to platforms like WhatsApp and other internet calling apps that people increasingly use for calls these days. With a future One UI release, Samsung looks ready to close that gap by expanding its Scam Detection features to third-party calling apps.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Scam Detection could soon work in WhatsApp, Telegram, and more 
 We found new strings in Samsung’s Call Assistant app v18.5.00.154, part of One UI 9.5 Beta 1, that extend Scam Detection beyond the Samsung Phone app to other voice calling apps.
